meta.title: Every Season — Vocabulary Set 3
meta.subject: English Vocabulary
meta.description: Vocabulary practice focusing on Week 11 words: summer, straw, barefoot, flutter, autumn, maple, winter, icicles.

questions.question: Which season is the hottest, when the sun shines strong and hot?
questions.explanation: Summer is the warmest season of the year, characterized by hot weather and sunshine.

questions.question: 'Winter' is the coldest season, bringing icicles and snowflakes.
questions.explanation: True. Winter is the cold season that comes after autumn.

questions.question: What are 'icicles'?
options: Dry plant stems used to make hats
Long pointed pieces of ice hanging down
questions.explanation: Icicles are hanging, pointed sticks of ice formed by freezing drips.

questions.question: Leaves turn colors and fall from trees in summer.
questions.explanation: False. Leaves turn color and fall in autumn (also called fall), not summer.

questions.question: Which word is a tree with leaves that turn orange or red in autumn?
questions.explanation: A maple is a tree famous for changing its leaves to orange, red, or yellow in autumn.

questions.question: If you take off your shoes and socks, you walk _______.
questions.hint: With no shoes or socks on.
questions.explanation: To walk barefoot means to walk with no shoes or socks on your feet.

questions.question: What does the verb 'flutter' describe in the summer story?
options: How frogs jump in the grass
How birds dive into ocean waves
How butterflies fly by moving wings quickly
How horses run to keep warm
questions.explanation: Butterflies flutter, which means they fly with light, quick movements of their wings.

questions.question: Sort these Week 11 words into Seasons or Nature things:
questions.explanation: Summer, autumn, and winter are seasons. Maples and icicles are natural structures.

questions.question: A 'straw' hat is made of dried plant stems.
questions.explanation: True. Straw is dried plant stems. A straw hat helps protect your head from the hot summer sun.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show how we walk in summer:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'We go barefoot in the grass.' It feels cool on a hot summer day.

questions.question: In which season does the wind whip and seeds scatter?
questions.explanation: Autumn (fall) is the season of windy days when leaves fall and seeds scatter.

questions.question: In autumn, leaves turn beautiful colors on the orange _______ tree.
questions.hint: A tree from our list that changes color in fall.
questions.explanation: The story mentions: 'Orange maple, red oak, yellow ash.'

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe what cold brings:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The cold brings winter icicles.' (Wait! Let's check the words: ['icicles', 'brings', 'cold', 'The', 'winter']. Yes, 'The cold brings winter icicles' uses all words).

questions.question: Icicles grow from the ground up like grass when it snows.
questions.explanation: False. Icicles are formed by dripping water that freezes, so they hang down from roofs, branches, or rocks.

questions.question: Why is summer described as the time to splash and swim?
options: Because it is very hot and water keeps us cool.
Because the ground is covered in ice and snow.
Because we wear thick jackets and hoods.
Because we want to gather acorns.
questions.explanation: Summer has a strong and hot sun. Splashing and swimming in water helps keep us cool when it is hot.
